A '''villager''' is a passive mob that trades with the player. Matcha Flavoured keeps the vanilla villager but replaces all of its [[trading|trades]], renames seven of its professions, gives each villager a [[favorite food]], and changes where new villagers come from.

== Spawning ==
[[Village]]s in Matcha Flavoured generate [[Abandoned village|abandoned]] from the pack's own building set, which contains no villagers, so the world has no villagers of its own.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/worldgen/structure/village_plains.json}}</ref> The developer wants the world to "feel abandoned until YOU come along", with villagers living at the player's base instead.<ref>{{Cite changelog|0.6-alpha|quote=I think the minecraft world should feel abandoned until YOU come along, so villagers at your base makes sense, it should feel alive. But the rest of the world shouldn't}}</ref>

The main source of villagers is the [[Asylum Seeker]] application sold by the [[Wandering Trader]], which spawns an adult or child villager with a randomly chosen culture (villager type). Villagers can then breed as in vanilla ''Minecraft''. Curing a {{MCW|Zombie Villager|zombie villager}} also works as in vanilla.

== Professions ==
{{Main|Trading#Professions}}
Villagers take a profession from the vanilla job site blocks. Seven professions have new names:

The names come from the resource pack's language file.<ref>{{Source|MF_resourcepack/assets/minecraft/lang/en_us.json}}</ref> Nitwits and unemployed villagers are unchanged.

== Behavior ==
=== Trading ===
{{Main|Trading}}
Villager trades can be used 999 times before restocking, and most sell goods in bulk for a single [[Obol]]. Apart from the [[Fisherman]], [[Jeweler]] and [[Weaponsmith]], villagers do not buy items from the player, except for one sale of their [[favorite food]].

An [[Amnestic]] placed next to a villager makes it forget its profession and return to Novice, so it can take a new job and new trades.

=== Favorite food ===
{{Main|Favorite food}}
Every employed villager that has been traded with at least once is given one extra trade: it buys 1 of a randomly chosen [[food]] (4 for chicken nuggets) for 1 obol, once.

=== Daily schedule ===
The pack stretches the vanilla villager schedule over a 72,000-tick cycle, three times the length of the vanilla 24,000-tick day, to match its longer [[Day and night|days]]. Adult villagers wake at tick 30, work from tick 6,000, meet from tick 27,000, idle from tick 33,000 and sleep from tick 36,000; every keyframe is exactly three times its vanilla value.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/minecraft/timeline/villager_schedule.json}}</ref>
{{Diagram|Villager schedule|caption=What adult and baby villagers do over one of the pack's days.}}

=== Protection ===
Villagers are counted as "villager friends" together with wandering traders, iron and snow golems, wolves, cats, happy ghasts and players. A [[Warding Stone]] gives every villager friend within 16 blocks {{EffectLink|Regeneration}} I for 3 seconds whenever they do not already have it.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/function/mechanics/warding_stone/effects.mcfunction}}</ref><ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/tags/entity_type/villager_friends.json}}</ref> The developer describes this as a "band-aid fix" for villagers, who "tend not to survive for too long on their own".<ref>{{Cite video|quote=Villagers are famously pacifist. They tend not to survive for too long on their own, so I added a band-aid fix for this.}}</ref>

== Advancements ==
* '''A True Community''': trade with every profession except the Weaponsmith. Rewards 5 obols.
* '''God help you...''' (hidden): "Commit great evil" by killing a villager or a wandering trader.<ref>{{Source|MF_datapack/data/matcha/advancement/tutorial/kill_villager.json}}</ref>
